newsitem.title: USA: Eleven development groups file Detroit casino bids.
newsitem.headline: Eleven development groups file Detroit casino bids.

text.p: Eleven groups filed bids Friday to open casino developments in Detroit, including Mirage Resorts Inc, which had dropped out of the running publicly weeks ago.
Detroit may have up to three land-based casinos under a statewide referendum approved last year that included preferences for local sponsors Atwater Group and Greektown Casino LLC.

Atwater filed a bid with Circus Circus Entertainment Inc and Greektown teamed with Millenium Management Co in their bid. Under the terms of the referendum, they would receive two of the licenses if they meet or exceed requirements.

Also filing a preliminary application were MGM Grand Inc ; Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc ; Casino America Inc with La Paloma LLC to operate an Isle of Capri casino; Rio Hotel & Casino Inc teamed with Paradise Valley LLC; Detroit businessman Don Barden, who operates the Majestic Star Casino in Gary, Ind.; Detroit Area Renewal Trust led by Lansing, Mich., businessman Joel Ferguson; Detroit Alive Casino Inc with President Charles Costa; and Detroit, Detroit LLC.
The city is scheduled to announce finalists for the three licenses Aug. 22. Mayor Dennis Archer hopes construction on the developments will begin in early 1998.
Each preliminary application includes a non-refundable $50,000 fee and each finalist will be required to submit a $250,000 fee.
